answer: Cross-chain identity binding at the relic: each identity must be attested on a second chain, so a sybil needs real capital locked on two ledgers. The signal is a signed beacon linking both addresses. Duplicating one identity costs 2x stake plus bridge fees, so an attacker farming n identities pays roughly n² across chains while rewards stay linear. The relic anchors provenance, the beacon enforces uniqueness. Returns go negative fast, which is why binding works.
